title: BigP3BCI Study L — 6x6 multi-paradigm (11 ALS subjects)
description: This derivative dataset comprises EEG recordings from 11 ALS patients participating in the BigP3BCI Study L, a multi-paradigm P300-based brain-computer interface investigation. The study employed a 6x6 character grid speller paradigm with 16-channel EEG recordings sampled at 256 Hz, designed to evaluate visual perception and target detection in a clinical population. This dataset represents a subset of the larger BigP3BCI initiative, the most comprehensive public P300 BCI dataset containing recordings from approximately 267 subjects across 20 studies.
methods_description: EEG data were acquired using a g.USBamp amplifier (g.tec) with 16 channels arranged in a standard 10-20 montage, sampled at 256 Hz with a 60 Hz line frequency. The experimental protocol employed a P300 paradigm using a 6x6 character grid speller with visual stimulus presentation. Each trial had a duration of 1.0 second, with events classified as Target or NonTarget stimuli. A calibration-then-test cross-validation approach was used for within-subject evaluation, with online feedback provided during the BCI application.
